en.name: Canterbury Cathedral
en.text: This magnificent UNESCO World Heritage site is the seat of the Archbishop of Canterbury and a masterpiece of English Gothic.

en.name: St Augustine's Abbey
en.text: The ruins of this former abbey date back to 598 AD and mark the very beginnings of Christianity in Anglo-Saxon England.

en.name: Westgate Towers
en.text: The largest surviving medieval gateway in England, it now houses a museum and offers panoramic views over the city.

en.name: Canterbury Roman Museum
en.text: Built around the remains of a Roman townhouse, this museum features stunning mosaics and a wealth of ancient artifacts.

en.name: The Beaney House of Art and Knowledge
en.text: A beautiful library and art gallery housed in a Victorian building, combining fine art with local historical collections.

en.name: Marlowe Theatre
en.text: A state-of-the-art theater on the riverside named after the playwright Christopher Marlowe, who was born in Canterbury.

en.name: Greyfriars Gardens
en.text: Peaceful riverside gardens on the Stour, home to the Greyfriars Chapel, the first Franciscan friary founded in England.

en.name: Christ Church Gate
en.text: The ornate main entrance to the cathedral precincts, built in the early 16th century and featuring elaborate sculptures.

en.name: Dane John Gardens
en.text: A historic park within the city walls, incorporating a Roman burial mound and offering scenic walking paths for visitors.

en.name: St Martin's Church
en.text: The oldest church in the English-speaking world still in use, predating the arrival of St Augustine in the 6th century.

descriptionAdvanced.de: Canterbury liegt am Fluss Stour in der Grafschaft Kent und ist eine der bedeutendsten historischen Städte Englands. Die Stadt blickt auf eine Siedlungsgeschichte zurück, die bis in die Eisenzeit reicht, wurde jedoch unter den Römern als Durovernum Cantiacorum zu einem wichtigen Verwaltungszentrum. Im Jahr 597 landete der Heilige Augustinus in Kent und machte Canterbury zum geistlichen Zentrum des Landes. Die Kathedrale von Canterbury, ein Meisterwerk der Gotik und Romanik, ist das Herzstück der Stadt und Ort des Martyriums von Thomas Becket im Jahr 1170. Dieses Ereignis machte die Stadt zu einem der wichtigsten Pilgerziele Europas, was später Geoffrey Chaucer zu seinem literarischen Klassiker inspirierte. Neben der Kathedrale gehören auch die Ruinen der St. Augustinus Abtei und die St. Martins Kirche zum UNESCO-Welterbe. Das Stadtbild ist geprägt von engen mittelalterlichen Gassen, Fachwerkhäusern und den Resten der römischen Stadtmauern. Heute ist Canterbury auch eine lebendige Universitätsstadt mit der University of Kent und dem Canterbury Christ Church University College. Die Kombination aus sakraler Pracht, akademischem Leben und touristischer Attraktivität verleiht der Stadt eine einzigartige Atmosphäre, die jährlich Millionen Besucher anzieht.
descriptionAdvanced.hu: Canterbury a Stour folyó partján, Kent megyében található, és Anglia egyik legjelentősebb történelmi városa. A település története a vaskorig nyúlik vissza, de a rómaiak alatt vált fontos közigazgatási központtá Durovernum Cantiacorum néven. 597-ben Szent Ágoston érkezett Kentbe, és Canterburyt tette meg az ország szellemi központjává. A canterburyi katedrális, a gótikus és román építészet remekműve, a város szíve és Thomas Becket 1170-es vértanúságának helyszíne. Ez az esemény tette a várost Európa egyik legfontosabb zarándokhelyévé, ami később Geoffrey Chaucert is megihlette irodalmi klasszikusa megírására. A katedrális mellett a Szent Ágoston-apátság romjai és a Szent Márton-templom is az UNESCO Világörökség részét képezi. A városképet szűk középkori utcák, favázas házak és a római városfalak maradványai határozzák meg. Ma Canterbury pezsgő egyetemi város is, itt működik a University of Kent és a Canterbury Christ Church University. A szakrális pompa, az akadémiai élet és a turisztikai vonzerő ötvözete egyedülálló hangulatot kölcsönöz a városnak, amely évente látogatók millióit vonzza.
descriptionAdvanced.ro: Canterbury este situat pe râul Stour în comitatul Kent și este unul dintre cele mai importante orașe istorice ale Angliei. Orașul are o istorie de așezare care datează din epoca fierului, dar a devenit un centru administrativ important sub romani ca Durovernum Cantiacorum. În anul 597, Sfântul Augustin a debarcat în Kent și a făcut din Canterbury centrul spiritual al țării. Catedrala din Canterbury, o capodoperă a stilurilor gotic și romanic, este inima orașului și locul martiriului lui Thomas Becket în 1170. Acest eveniment a transformat orașul într-una dintre cele mai importante destinații de pelerinaj din Europa, inspirându-l ulterior pe Geoffrey Chaucer pentru clasicul său literar. Pe lângă catedrală, ruinele Abației Sf. Augustin și Biserica Sf. Martin fac parte din Patrimoniul Mondial UNESCO. Peisajul urban este caracterizat de străzi medievale înguste, case cu structură de lemn și resturi ale zidurilor romane. Astăzi, Canterbury este și un oraș universitar vibrant, cu University of Kent și Canterbury Christ Church University. Combinația de splendoare sacră, viață academică și atracție turistică conferă orașului o atmosferă unică ce atrage anual milioane de vizitatori.
descriptionAdvanced.en: Canterbury is situated on the River Stour in the county of Kent and is one of England's most significant historic cities. The town has a settlement history dating back to the Iron Age but became a major administrative center under the Romans as Durovernum Cantiacorum. In the year 597, Saint Augustine landed in Kent and established Canterbury as the country's spiritual center. Canterbury Cathedral, a masterpiece of Gothic and Romanesque architecture, is the heart of the city and the site of Thomas Becket's martyrdom in 1170. This event made the city one of Europe's primary pilgrimage destinations, later inspiring Geoffrey Chaucer's literary classic. Along with the cathedral, the ruins of St Augustine's Abbey and St Martin's Church are part of the UNESCO World Heritage site. The cityscape is defined by narrow medieval streets, timber-framed houses, and the remains of Roman city walls. Today, Canterbury is also a lively university city, home to the University of Kent and Canterbury Christ Church University. The combination of sacred grandeur, academic life, and tourist appeal gives the city a unique atmosphere that attracts millions of visitors annually.
